comparator.name: Chemistry
comparator.route: Chemistry of Life specialisation with University Minor
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations give a 60 EC common first year, 50 EC upper-year core, 20 EC specialisation, a 5 EC Research Practical, a 15 EC research project and a 30 EC minor. Chemistry of Life is first in the formal specialisation list. No specialisation is designated as the general route. The University Minor is shown as open choice.
components: Linear Algebra & Multivariable Calculus for Chemistry
Chemistry & Society: Ethical and Professional Aspects
Compulsory experimental research project; entry requires the completed first year and at least 130 EC in the curriculum.
Genuine 30-EC minor space preserved without inventing a subject.

routeSelection.route: Chemistry of Life specialisation with University Minor
routeSelection.basis: The generic Chemistry target offers three formally named 20-EC specialisations. Current official evidence does not establish one as more representative or less specialised than the others, so the first specialisation in the formally adopted 2026–2027 regulations, Chemistry of Life, is selected as the neutral tie-break. The University Minor preserves the regulated open 30-EC minor space. Neither choice is based on UCR fit.

core: Molecular structure, biochemistry, cellular mechanisms and Chemistry of Life applications
Biomedical function, disease, pharmacology and molecular health research as related applications of molecular science
Mathematics, programming, modelling and statistical analysis for molecular and material questions
Laboratory experimentation and independent scientific inquiry
Materials, energy, sustainability, catalysis, resources and environmental consequences of chemical systems
questions: How do molecular and biochemical processes produce biological function, disease and treatment possibilities?
How can molecular and biomedical questions be investigated experimentally and quantitatively?
How can materials, energy and resource systems be studied for sustainability and environmental improvement?

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biomedical life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work, genetics, disease, pharmacology and quantitative analysis form the visible spine; the title does not imply a chemistry degree.
alternatives.concept: Study biomolecules, cells and disease through biochemistry, molecular biology, laboratory work and pharmacology. Add chemistry and materials foundations, geochemistry and quantitative methods to investigate how molecular processes work.
progression: Life-science, brain and behaviour, mathematics and sustainability foundations precede biochemistry, environmental geochemistry and molecular laboratory work. Pathology, immunity, pharmacology and resource recovery extend the scientific core. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, environmental materials & quantitative science
alternatives.concept: Study how materials and resources move through environmental systems. Combine geochemistry, soils, life-cycle analysis and resource recovery with biochemistry and quantitative modelling.
alternatives.labelReason: Four molecular or biochemical courses, twelve environmental, Earth, materials and sustainability courses, and seven mathematics, programming, data and research courses support the three stated strands in proportion.
progression: Sustainability, mathematics, programming and life-science foundations precede biochemistry, soils, linear systems and numerical methods. Geochemistry, resource recovery, renewable design and Earth resources extend the materials strand. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.
alternatives.distinctness: 11 courses and 82.5 EC differ in each direction. This option emphasises environmental materials, field evidence and renewable systems. The first emphasises cells, physiology, pathology, immunity and pharmacology.

candidates.label: Biochemistry, environmental materials and quantitative science
Synthetic, inorganic and physical chemistry
candidates.rationale: The current UCR sciences offer relevant chemical principles, measurement and experiments in selected contexts but do not form a cumulative sequence in organic and inorganic synthesis, physical and quantum chemistry, spectroscopy and chemical analysis.

selection.assessment: The two supported directions are coherent and substantially distinct. A third synthetic, inorganic and physical chemistry direction lacks sustained specialist chemistry content and laboratory progression. This limitation concerns academic scope, independently of timetabling.

blocks: Both directly study biomolecules, metabolism and biochemical mechanisms; UCR does so within life science rather than a chemistry sequence.
Both study processes within cells. UCR takes a molecular cell-biology perspective; Groningen emphasises chemical and quantitative approaches.
Both use molecular and biochemical laboratory approaches. The UCR course covers a wider set of life-science techniques, while Groningen focuses on recombinant DNA and biotechnology.
Both introduce chemical analysis and spectroscopy concepts through scientific exercises. UCR also covers waves and materials in a sustainability context.
Both provide mathematical foundations for scientific study; UCR is a broad methods course rather than chemistry-specific mathematics.
Advanced Calculus directly develops multivariable calculus and differential equations, while the comparator component also integrates linear algebra for chemistry.
Chemistry core, laboratory research & open minor
UCR has no chemical transport-phenomena course.
UCR has no synthesis and chemical-analysis laboratory.
UCR has one broad life-science laboratory but no combined biochemistry and physical-chemistry practical.
UCR Earth-material courses do not reproduce general inorganic chemistry.
UCR environmental and lifecycle courses do not reproduce molecular physical-properties-of-materials study.
UCR has no advanced organic chemistry.
UCR has no second synthesis laboratory.
UCR has no advanced physical chemistry.
UCR has no soft-molecular-materials chemistry course.
The comparator’s chemistry-specific ethical and professional component remains unmatched; generic academic orientation is not presented as chemistry training.
UCR pharmacology includes toxicity but does not reproduce a dedicated chemical-toxicity and safety course.
UCR has no advanced chemical or biochemical synthesis-and-analysis sequence.
UCR offers laboratory and applied research courses, but no staged chemistry research practical.
The compulsory experimental Chemistry research project remains visible; UCR’s standardized optional independent-research opportunity is shown here without claiming a scheduled equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC University Minor remains open; no fixed UCR content is invented for it.
UCR life science introduces biomolecules and their functions. Groningen studies molecular structure and reactivity across chemistry.
Groningen uses chemical tools to study and modify biomolecules. UCR Pharmacology studies drug action and its effects.
Groningen studies energy metabolism and biomass conversion at molecular scale. UCR examines energy systems and resource use.

notes.text: Groningen requires organic, inorganic, physical and quantum chemistry, spectroscopy and a sequence of synthesis and analysis laboratories. UCR options cover selected molecular, biochemical and environmental applications.
Groningen also requires a 20 EC specialisation, a research practical and a 15 EC experimental chemistry project. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the scheduled study plan.

audience.programmeDescription: Chemistry at the University of Groningen studies how substances are structured, how they react and how they can be analysed. The degree includes practical laboratory work, a specialisation, a minor and an experimental research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options share some biochemical and quantitative study with Groningen. The closest option focuses on molecular life science and disease. The second applies related science to environmental materials and resources.
